newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: MANILA T-BILL RATES HIGHER DUE TO PESO VOLATILITY.
newsitem.headline: MANILA T-BILL RATES HIGHER DUE TO PESO VOLATILITY.

text.p: Secondary treasury bill rates rose on Wednesday as banks took a defensive stance following the renewed volatility of the peso, traders said.
Banks, however, were not keen on buying bills, they said.
"The demand for bills had died down," a trader said, since banks believed interest rates could rise again in the coming days as a strategy to defend the peso from speculative attack.
"Banks just want to see what's happening at the Philippine Dealing System (PDS)," another said. The PDS is the electronic board for the peso-dollar exchange market.
The peso came under pressure following the continued turmoil in the region's currencies. It had fallen to an intra-day low of 29.10 to dollar in mid-morning trade.
Traders said any T-bill buying was limited to service corporate requirements where appetite is on short-term bills of three months or lower.
A Reuters poll of five banks gave offer rates of 13.875/14.10 percent for the three-month bills; 14/14.25 percent for the six months; and 14.125/14.375 percent for the one-year bills.
The average interbank call loan rate was steady at 18.0625 percent, with 36 lenders and 23 borrowers.
Volume was higher at 23.32 billion pesos from 18.24 billion.
